title: Extending the Bloch sphere model to an N-qubit system
authors: Francisco Piñero, Cristian Franco, Hernán I. de la Cruz, Fernando L. Pelayo, Vicente Pascual, Mauro Mezzini, Jose Javier Paulet, Fernando Cuartero
abstract: The Bloch sphere is an elegant tool for representing single-qubit states. However, a widely accepted generalization for multi-qubit systems with entanglement remains absent. We propose a novel geometric model extending the Bloch sphere representation to arbitrary $N$-qubit systems using $2^N-1$ spheres. We demonstrate that any pure 2-qubit state is uniquely described by three spheres: two for individual qubits and a third encapsulating bipartite entanglement. Generalizing this, we establish an $N$-qubit parameterization through the hierarchical application of controlled rotation gates along the $Z$ and $Y$ axes. We formally prove a strict bijection between the standard state vector representation and our model's angular parameters. This framework provides an intuitive visualization of multiple entanglement, offering potential computational advantages for quantum simulators and new analytical perspectives on quantum gates.
summary: This paper introduces a novel geometric framework to represent N-qubit quantum states by extending the Bloch sphere concept into 2N-1 interconnected spheres. It rigorously proves that this model provides a unique, bijective parameterization for any pure multi-qubit state. This offers an intuitive visualization and computational structure for analyzing entanglement in complex quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the lack of a widely accepted, intuitive geometric model to represent multi-qubit quantum states that incorporate entanglement, extending beyond the single-qubit Bloch sphere.
main_result: The authors propose and prove a novel framework showing that an arbitrary N-qubit pure state can be uniquely parameterized using exactly 2N-1 spheres, providing a strict bijection to the standard state vector representation.
method: The methodology involves generalizing the geometric concept of the Bloch sphere by deriving parameterizations for two and three qubits based on controlled rotation gates. This leads to establishing a unique normal form for the state vector through sequential phase elimination and amplitude setting using unitary transformations.
